base.source_text:
## What are cells
Cells are the basic units of life.
All living things are made up of one or more cells and carry out three basic processes: Nutrition, Reproduction and interaction:
- Nutrition: Living things need energy to stay alive. To obtain it, they eat different kinds of food.
- Interaction: Living things detect changes in their environment and respond to them.
- Reproduction: All living things are able to copy themselves in order to secure their DNA for the future.
Most of them are very small, they can only be seen through a microscope but they still can differ in size.
For example, brain cells, known as neurons, are much bigger than red blood cells.
Cells can also differ in shape. They can be round, elongated, flat, star-shaped, etc.
Our body is made up of different cells

## Types of cells
Types of cells: Eukaryotic and Prokaryotic
- Eukaryotic: It has a nucleus. The DNA (instructions for cells) is in the nucleus. Multicellular or unicellular organisms. Examples: animals and plants.
- Prokaryotic: It doesn't have a nucleus. The DNA is floating in the cytoplasm. Unicellular organisms. Examples: bacteria.

## Parts of a cell
- Membrane: A thin layer that surrounds and protects the cell.
- Nucleus: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell and contains the DNA.
- Cytoplasm: A jelly-like substance, mostly made of water, that contains the organelles.
- Organelles: An organelle is a tiny cellular structure that performs specific functions within a cell. Organelles are embedded within the cytoplasm. In more complex cells, organelles are often enclosed by their own membrane.

## Organelles and their functions
- Organelle: Nucleus. Responsible for: Housing DNA, "Brain" of the cell.
- Organelle: Mitochondria. Responsible for: Energy production, "powerhouse" of the cell.
- Organelle: Golgi apparatus. Responsible for: Sorting, packaging and transport of proteins.
- Organelle: Endoplasmic reticulum. Responsible for: Carries proteins through the cell.
- Organelle: Chloroplast. Responsible for: Photosynthesis, only present in plants.
- Organelle: Flagellum. Responsible for: Locomotion and sensory functions.
- Organelle: Vacuole. Responsible for: Storage.
- Organelle: Lysosome. Responsible for: Digestion of large molecules.
- Organelle: Centrioles. Responsible for: Cell division.
- Organelle: Ribosome. Responsible for: Makes proteins.

Parts of the cell: Mitochondria
Mitochondria receive the nutrients and oxygen, and it make the energy the cell needs.

Lysosomes
They get rid of waste material from the cell. They can also destroy bacteria and viruses.

Ribosomes
Ribosomes make proteins for the cells. Do you remember why proteins are important? They repair any damage caused.

Golgi body
It sorts, packages and transports proteins inside and outside the cell. It is the Amazon of the cell.

Vacuole
Before the cell needs the nutrients, what happens with them? And where is the waste? They are in the vacuole. It is a place where the cell stores food, water, and waste.

## Animal and plant cells
Both animal and plant cells have 3 main parts: Membrane, Nucleus and Cytoplasm (with organelles).
Animal and plant cells are different:
- Plant cells have specialised organelles called chloroplasts.
- Chloroplasts absorb sunlight and contain chlorophyll (which gives plants their green color).
- Plant cells are usually larger and more regular in shape. Plant cells have a rigid cell wall.
- Plant cells usually have only one big vacuole, while animal cells have many tiny vacuoles (called vesicles).
Plant cell: Chloroplasts
Chloroplasts help plants carry out photosynthesis. Inside the chloroplasts, chlorophyll captures energy from sunlight.

Animal cells are mostly round and irregular in shape while plant cells have rectangular shapes.
Plant cells have a rigid cell wall that surrounds the cell membrane and gives them their shape.

## Living Things Organization

Multicellular living things are made up of different types of cells.

Cells: The cells work together at different levels.

A tissue is a group of cells with a function.

An organ is a group of tissues with a common function.

In a unicellular living thing, such as a bacterium, there is only the first level of organization, the cell. This one cell has to carry out all the functions of the living thing.

Multicellular living things are made up of different cells. These are called levels of organisation.

Tissues: Groups of the same type of cells join together to form tissues. Animals have muscle tissue, which consists of muscle cells. Plants have an epidermis - the tissue that covers leaves - which consists of epidermal cells.

Organs: Tissues join together to form organs. Tissues in organs work together to perform a common function. Muscles, bones, the heart and the lungs are animal organs. Leaves and flowers are plant organs.

Systems: Organs are grouped to form systems. Organs in systems work together to perform a common function such as moving our body or obtaining the nutrients we need to live.

Organisms: Finally, all the different systems work together to form an organism, a living thing.

## Exercise 5: Unit 1 Challenge

A. Circle the correct answer.
1. Which organelle controls the cell?
a) Ribosome
b) Nucleus
c) Vacuole

2. Which organelle produces energy?
a) Mitochondria
b) Golgi apparatus
c) Lysosome

3. Which cells have chloroplasts?
a) Animal cells
b) Plant cells
c) Blood cells

4. Which organisms have only one cell?
a) Multicellular organisms
b) Unicellular organisms
c) Plants

5. Which level comes after tissues?
a) Systems
b) Organs
c) Organism

B. Write TRUE or FALSE.
1. Animal cells have a cell wall.
2. Plant cells have chloroplasts.
3. Lysosomes remove waste.
4. Ribosomes make proteins.
5. Systems are made of organs.

C. Write one sentence about each concept.

1.summary_md:
## What are cells
Cells are the basic units of life. All living things have cells.
Living things do three processes:
- **Nutrition**: They get energy from food.
- **Interaction**: They respond to changes.
- **Reproduction**: They make copies of DNA.
Cells are very small. We use a **microscope** to see them.
Cells have different sizes. **Neurons** are bigger than red blood cells.
Cells have different shapes. They can be round, flat, or star-shaped.

💡 Las células son como los ladrillos de un castillo. Aunque son muy pequeños, se unen para formar todo tu cuerpo, y cada uno tiene una forma diferente según lo que necesite hacer.

## Types of cells
There are two types of cells:
- **Eukaryotic**: It has a **nucleus** with DNA. They can be in animals and plants.
- **Prokaryotic**: It does not have a nucleus. DNA floats in the **cytoplasm**. Example: **bacteria**.

💡 Piensa en las células eucariotas como una oficina del director donde guardan los papeles importantes (el núcleo). Las procariotas son como una habitación abierta donde los papeles están sobre la mesa.

## Parts of a cell
A cell has four main parts:
- **Membrane**: A thin layer that protects the cell.
- **Nucleus**: It controls the cell and has the DNA.
- **Cytoplasm**: A jelly liquid with water.
- **Organelles**: Tiny structures that do specific jobs inside the cell.

💡 Imagina que la célula es una casa. La membrana es la puerta con llave, el núcleo es la cocina de control, el citoplasma es el aire de la casa, y los orgánulos son los electrodomésticos que trabajan.

test.explain_es: Las células son las unidades básicas de la vida.

test.q: How many cells are living things made of?
test.explain_es: Todos los seres vivos están formados por una o más células.

test.q: What are the three basic life processes?
test.explain_es: Los tres procesos básicos son nutrición, interacción y reproducción.

test.q: Why do living things need nutrition?
test.explain_es: Los seres vivos necesitan energía para mantenerse vivos a través de la nutrición.

test.q: What do living things do in interaction?
test.explain_es: La interacción significa detectar cambios en el entorno y responder a ellos.
La reproducción permite copiar el ADN para el futuro.

test.q: How can we see most cells?
test.explain_es: La mayoría de las células son muy pequeñas y solo se ven con un microscopio.
Las células del cerebro se conocen como neuronas.
Las células pueden tener diferentes formas como redondas, planas o en forma de estrella.

test.q: What are the two main types of cells?
test.explain_es: Los dos tipos de células son eucariotas y procariotas.

test.q: Does a Eukaryotic cell have a nucleus?
test.explain_es: La célula eucariota tiene un núcleo donde está el ADN.

test.q: Give an example of Eukaryotic cells.
test.explain_es: Los animales y las plantas son ejemplos de organismos con células eucariotas.

test.q: Does a Prokaryotic cell have a nucleus?
test.explain_es: La célula procariota no tiene núcleo y el ADN flota en el citoplasma.

test.q: What is an example of a Prokaryotic cell?
test.explain_es: Las bacterias son un claro ejemplo de células procariotas.
La membrana es una capa fina que rodea y protege la célula.
El núcleo controla las actividades de la célula y contiene el ADN.
El citoplasma es una sustancia gelatinosa, hecha sobre todo de agua, que contiene orgánulos.

options: A tiny cellular structure with a function
test.explain_es: Un orgánulo es una estructura celular diminuta que realiza funciones específicas.

parts.name: Cell membrane
parts.text_es: Soy como la puerta de una casa que decide quién entra y sale.
parts.body_en: I protect the cell and let good things inside.
parts.body_es: Protejo la célula y dejo entrar lo bueno.
parts.clue_en: I am the outer layer that protects the whole cell.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.text_es: Soy como el jefe que da las órdenes en una fábrica.
parts.body_en: I direct all cell activities to keep the body working.
parts.body_es: Dirijo todas las actividades para que el cuerpo funcione.
parts.clue_en: I am the center that gives orders to the cell.

parts.name: Mitochondria
parts.text_es: Soy como una pequeña pila que da energía.
parts.body_en: I give energy for nutrition and life.
parts.body_es: Doy energía para la nutrición y la vida.
parts.clue_en: I produce energy for the cell.

story.en: Food and energy arrive at the cell membrane.
story.es: La comida y la energía llegan a la membrana celular.

story.en: The nucleus receives the signal and gives orders.
story.es: El núcleo recibe la señal y da órdenes.

story.en: The mitochondria make energy for the whole cell.
story.es: Las mitocondrias fabrican energía para toda la célula.

parts.name: Eukaryotic cell
parts.text_es: Es una célula grande y compleja como una casa grande.
parts.body_en: It has a nucleus to protect DNA.
parts.body_es: Tiene un núcleo para guardar las instrucciones.
parts.clue_en: I have a safe room for my DNA.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.text_es: Es el jefe que guarda los planos.
parts.body_en: It stores DNA safely.
parts.body_es: Guarda el ADN de forma segura.
parts.clue_en: I keep the central instructions inside.

parts.name: Prokaryotic cell
parts.text_es: Es una célula pequeña y sencilla.
parts.body_en: It has no nucleus.
parts.body_es: No tiene núcleo cerrado.
parts.clue_en: I do not have walls around my DNA.

parts.name: DNA
parts.text_es: Son las instrucciones para la vida.
parts.body_en: It tells the cell what to do.
parts.body_es: Dice a la célula lo que debe hacer.
parts.clue_en: I am the secret recipe inside.

story.en: The traveler visits the big eukaryotic cell.
story.es: El viajero visita la gran célula eucariota.

1.text:
## What are cells
Cells are the basic units of life.
All living things are made up of one or more cells and carry out three basic processes: Nutrition, Reproduction and interaction:
- Nutrition: Living things need energy to stay alive. To obtain it, they eat different kinds of food.
- Interaction: Living things detect changes in their environment and respond to them.
- Reproduction: All living things are able to copy themselves in order to secure their DNA for the future.
Most of them are very small, they can only be seen through a microscope but they still can differ in size.
For example, brain cells, known as neurons, are much bigger than red blood cells.
Cells can also differ in shape. They can be round, elongated, flat, star-shaped, etc.
Our body is made up of different cells

## Types of cells
Types of cells: Eukaryotic and Prokaryotic
- Eukaryotic: It has a nucleus. The DNA (instructions for cells) is in the nucleus. Multicellular or unicellular organisms. Examples: animals and plants.
- Prokaryotic: It doesn't have a nucleus. The DNA is floating in the cytoplasm. Unicellular organisms. Examples: bacteria.

## Parts of a cell
- Membrane: A thin layer that surrounds and protects the cell.
- Nucleus: The nucleus controls the activities of the cell and contains the DNA.
- Cytoplasm: A jelly-like substance, mostly made of water, that contains the organelles.
- Organelles: An organelle is a tiny cellular structure that performs specific functions within a cell. Organelles are embedded within the cytoplasm. In more complex cells, organelles are often enclosed by their own membrane.

2.text:
## Organelles and their functions
- Organelle: Nucleus. Responsible for: Housing DNA, "Brain" of the cell.
- Organelle: Mitochondria. Responsible for: Energy production, "powerhouse" of the cell.
- Organelle: Golgi apparatus. Responsible for: Sorting, packaging and transport of proteins.
- Organelle: Endoplasmic reticulum. Responsible for: Carries proteins through the cell.
- Organelle: Chloroplast. Responsible for: Photosynthesis, only present in plants.
- Organelle: Flagellum. Responsible for: Locomotion and sensory functions.
- Organelle: Vacuole. Responsible for: Storage.
- Organelle: Lysosome. Responsible for: Digestion of large molecules.
- Organelle: Centrioles. Responsible for: Cell division.
- Organelle: Ribosome. Responsible for: Makes proteins.

Parts of the cell: Mitochondria
Mitochondria receive the nutrients and oxygen, and it make the energy the cell needs.

Lysosomes
They get rid of waste material from the cell. They can also destroy bacteria and viruses.

Ribosomes
Ribosomes make proteins for the cells. Do you remember why proteins are important? They repair any damage caused.

Golgi body
It sorts, packages and transports proteins inside and outside the cell. It is the Amazon of the cell.

Vacuole
Before the cell needs the nutrients, what happens with them? And where is the waste? They are in the vacuole. It is a place where the cell stores food, water, and waste.

## Animal and plant cells
Both animal and plant cells have 3 main parts: Membrane, Nucleus and Cytoplasm (with organelles).
Animal and plant cells are different:
- Plant cells have specialised organelles called chloroplasts.
- Chloroplasts absorb sunlight and contain chlorophyll (which gives plants their green color).
- Plant cells are usually larger and more regular in shape. Plant cells have a rigid cell wall.
- Plant cells usually have only one big vacuole, while animal cells have many tiny vacuoles (called vesicles).
Plant cell: Chloroplasts
Chloroplasts help plants carry out photosynthesis. Inside the chloroplasts, chlorophyll captures energy from sunlight.

Animal cells are mostly round and irregular in shape while plant cells have rectangular shapes.
Plant cells have a rigid cell wall that surrounds the cell membrane and gives them their shape.

3.text:
## Living Things Organization
Multicellular living things are made up of different types of cells.

Cells: The cells work together at different levels.

A tissue is a group of cells with a function.

An organ is a group of tissues with a common function.

In a unicellular living thing, such as a bacterium, there is only the first level of organization, the cell. This one cell has to carry out all the functions of the living thing.

Multicellular living things are made up of different cells. These are called levels of organisation.

Tissues: Groups of the same type of cells join together to form tissues. Animals have muscle tissue, which consists of muscle cells. Plants have an epidermis - the tissue that covers leaves - which consists of epidermal cells.

Organs: Tissues join together to form organs. Tissues in organs work together to perform a common function. Muscles, bones, the heart and the lungs are animal organs. Leaves and flowers are plant organs.

Systems: Organs are grouped to form systems. Organs in systems work together to perform a common function such as moving our body or obtaining the nutrients we need to live.

Organisms: Finally, all the different systems work together to form an organism, a living thing.

## Exercise 5: Unit 1 Challenge
A. Circle the correct answer.
1. Which organelle controls the cell?
a) Ribosome
b) Nucleus
c) Vacuole

2. Which organelle produces energy?
a) Mitochondria
b) Golgi apparatus
c) Lysosome

3. Which cells have chloroplasts?
a) Animal cells
b) Plant cells
c) Blood cells

4. Which organisms have only one cell?
a) Multicellular organisms
b) Unicellular organisms
c) Plants

5. Which level comes after tissues?
a) Systems
b) Organs
c) Organism

B. Write TRUE or FALSE.
1. Animal cells have a cell wall.
2. Plant cells have chloroplasts.
3. Lysosomes remove waste.
4. Ribosomes make proteins.
5. Systems are made of organs.

parts.name: Nucleus
parts.says_en: I am the brain and I keep the DNA safe!
parts.text_en: The nucleus is the control center of the cell.
parts.text_es: El núcleo es como el cerebro o la oficina del director que guarda todos los planos.
parts.body_en: It controls all activities and stores the cell instructions.
parts.body_es: Controla todas las actividades y guarda las instrucciones para que la célula funcione bien.
parts.clue_en: I am the big dome that holds the DNA.

parts.name: Membrane
parts.says_en: I protect the cell from danger outside!
parts.text_en: The membrane is a thin layer around the cell.
parts.text_es: La membrana es como la muralla de un castillo con puertas de seguridad.
parts.body_en: It surrounds and protects the cell from the outside.
parts.body_es: Rodea y protege la célula, decidiendo qué entra y qué sale.
parts.clue_en: I am the outer edge that protects everything.

parts.name: Cytoplasm
parts.says_en: I am the jelly where everything floats!
parts.text_en: The cytoplasm is a jelly-like substance full of water.
parts.text_es: El citoplasma es como una piscina de gelatina transparente donde flotan las cosas.
parts.body_en: It holds all the tiny organelles in place.
parts.body_es: Mantiene todos los orgánulos en su sitio y permite que se muevan.
parts.clue_en: I am the dark jelly filling the cell space.

parts.name: Mitochondria
parts.says_en: I make energy to keep us running!
parts.text_en: Mitochondria are tiny power plants inside the cell.
parts.text_es: La mitocondria es como una pequeña central eléctrica que da energía.
parts.body_en: They produce energy for all cell activities.
parts.body_es: Producen la energía necesaria para que la célula pueda trabajar.
parts.clue_en: I am the oval shape with a yellow zigzag inside.

parts.name: Organelles
parts.says_en: We do all the hard work here!
parts.text_en: Organelles are tiny structures that perform special tasks.
parts.text_es: Los orgánulos son como pequeñas herramientas y fábricas dentro de la célula.
parts.body_en: They help the cell live, grow and make things.
parts.body_es: Ayudan a que la célula realice todas sus funciones vitales.
parts.clue_en: We are the folded tubes and dots making things.

story.en: The traveler enters safely through the cell membrane.
story.es: La viajera entra de forma segura a través de la membrana celular.

story.en: She swims across the soft jelly cytoplasm.
story.es: Nada a través del suave citoplasma en forma de gelatina.

story.en: She visits the big nucleus to see the DNA plans.
story.es: Visita el gran núcleo para ver los planos del ADN.

story.en: She watches the busy organelles building proteins.
story.es: Observa a los ocupados orgánulos construyendo proteínas.

story.en: Finally, she gets a boost of energy from the mitochondria.
story.es: Finalmente, recibe un impulso de energía de la mitocondria.

1.outro_es: ¡Así es como una célula trabaja unida como un gran equipo para mantenernos vivos!
